purpose: Create a Linux TAP device for Firecracker to attach to. The TAP must exist on the host before PUT /network-interfaces references it.

flags.name: mode tap
flags.doc: Required — Firecracker uses TAP, not TUN.

examples.invocation: sudo ip tuntap add tap0 mode tap; sudo ip addr add 172.16.0.1/30 dev tap0; sudo ip link set tap0 up

purpose: Enable IPv4 forwarding on the host. Required for any NAT-based or bridge-based microVM routing.

command: nft add rule <table> postrouting ip saddr <guest-ip> oifname <host-iface> counter masquerade
purpose: Create the NAT masquerade rule that rewrites guest packets' source IP to the host's egress interface IP. The kernel's outbound side of the NAT-routing pattern.

examples.invocation: sudo nft add table firecracker; sudo nft 'add chain firecracker postrouting { type nat hook postrouting priority srcnat; policy accept; }'; sudo nft add rule firecracker postrouting ip saddr 172.16.0.2 oifname eth0 counter masquerade
examples.expected_output: Rule installed; outbound guest traffic gets host's source IP

purpose: Equivalent to the nft masquerade rule via the iptables-nft compat layer. Use only if your tooling/familiarity prefers iptables syntax (nft is recommended for production).

examples.invocation: sudo iptables-nft -t nat -A POSTROUTING -o eth0 -s 172.16.0.2 -j MASQUERADE; sudo iptables-nft -A FORWARD -i tap0 -o eth0 -j ACCEPT

command: ip route add default via <tap-ip> dev eth0 (in guest)
purpose: Inside the guest, configure the default route through the TAP IP. Combined with `ip addr add <guest-ip>/30 dev eth0` and `ip link set eth0 up`, gives the guest egress.

examples.invocation: ip addr add 172.16.0.2/30 dev eth0; ip link set eth0 up; ip route add default via 172.16.0.1 dev eth0
examples.expected_output: Guest can route to internet (assuming host has it)
examples.scenario: Guest-side networking init (typically in init script)

purpose: From INSIDE the guest, mint an MMDS V2 session token. TTL between 1 and 21600 seconds. Returns the token as plaintext body.

examples.expected_output: Plaintext token; subsequent GETs use X-metadata-token: $TOKEN

purpose: From INSIDE the guest, fetch an MMDS resource. Path is a JSON Pointer into the MMDS data store.

flags.name: Accept
flags.doc: Output format selector. plain/text returns AWS IMDS format.

flags.name: X-metadata-token
flags.doc: Required for V2; ignored for V1.
